questions.q: What happens to data stored in an emptyDir volume when its Pod is deleted?
options: It is automatically migrated to a PersistentVolume
It is deleted along with the Pod — emptyDir provides no durability beyond the Pod's own lifetime
It is backed up to the cluster's etcd store
It persists and can be reattached to a new Pod later
questions.explain: emptyDir storage is created when the Pod starts and removed when the Pod is deleted — it survives a container crash within the Pod but not the Pod's own deletion.

questions.q: What is the relationship between a PersistentVolume (PV) and a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC)?
options: A PVC is a cluster-level resource and a PV is a namespaced request
A PV represents actual cluster storage; a PVC is a namespaced request for storage that Kubernetes binds to a matching PV
They are two names for the same object
A Pod mounts a PV directly and a PVC is only used for monitoring
questions.explain: A PV is the cluster-level representation of real storage. A PVC is a request (namespaced) for storage meeting certain criteria, and Kubernetes binds it to a satisfying PV.

questions.q: In a Pod spec, how does a Pod actually reference durable storage backed by a PersistentVolume?
options: By referencing the PersistentVolume's name directly in volumes.persistentVolume
By mounting the PersistentVolumeClaim via volumes.persistentVolumeClaim.claimName, not the PV directly
By specifying the raw cloud disk ID in the container spec
PersistentVolumes cannot be mounted by Pods at all
questions.explain: Pods mount the claim (PVC), not the PV directly. This indirection means the Pod spec never needs to know the underlying storage technology.

questions.q: Northbridge's product-catalog database needs exclusive read-write access from a single node at a time. Which accessMode fits?
options: ReadOnlyMany
ReadWriteMany
ReadWriteOnce
WriteOnlyOnce
questions.explain: ReadWriteOnce allows read-write mounting from a single node at a time — the typical mode for a database's persistent storage.

questions.q: What does persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain mean for a PersistentVolume once its claim is deleted?
options: The underlying storage and its data are automatically deleted
The underlying storage and its data are kept, requiring manual cleanup rather than automatic deletion
The PV is automatically rebound to a new, random PVC
Retain has no effect on storage behavior
questions.explain: Retain preserves the underlying storage and data after the claim is released, leaving cleanup to be done manually — as opposed to Delete, which removes the storage automatically.
